reason: Both conversations correctly identify the crushed, fluff-filled vent hose as the cause of thermostat cycling and neither pushes an internal part. Conversation 1 is more efficient (resolved in three turns), gives the clearer safety boundary ('do not keep running it while it is overheating', unplug before handling, stay nearby for the test run) and lays out a sensible fallback escalation if it still trips with a clear vent. Conversation 2 earns credit for the confirming hose-off test and for honestly telling the tenant a new hose isn't necessarily needed and to inform the landlord, but it needlessly prompted for a model number to source a replacement hose for what is a generic accessory, drifted to a 'wall vent outside' the customer never described, and gave no plan if the fault persisted.
